newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea to send N.Korean sailor back home.
newsitem.headline: South Korea to send N.Korean sailor back home.

text.p: South Korea will return home a North Korean sailor rescued while drifting off a Southern island, the Seoul Defence Ministry said on Saturday.

It is the first goodwill gesture by South Korea towards the North since tense relations between the two Koreas turned icy after a North Korean submarine landed 26 agents on a South Korean beach in September.

A Defence Ministry statement said the North Korean sailor, identified as Chung Kwang-son of the Stalinist state's navy, was picked up by a South Korean maritime police vessel and taken to the western port city of Inchon on Saturday.

"Our government plans to return the rescued North Korean soldier shortly through the Military Armistice Commission on humanitarian grounds and in accordance with his own free will," the statement said.
The commission overseas a truce signed in 1953 at the end of three-year Korean War.

Chung's steel boat drifted south from North Korea and was first spotted on Friday about 21 miles southwest of South Korea's So Yonpyongdo island, which is close to the border with the communist North, South Korean police said.
